paper_title: Corner contribution to the entanglement in two-dimensional systems: A tensor network perspective (Feldman, 2026, arXiv)
core_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Claim.} For a normalized pure state represented by an iPEPS with uniform bond dimension \(\chi\), if a bipartition boundary cuts exactly \(k\) virtual legs, then the Schmidt rank \(N\) and von Neumann entropy \(S(A)\) obey
\[
S(A)\leq \log N\leq k\log\chi.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &|\psi\rangle_{AB}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\psi_i |i\rangle_A |i\rangle_B,
\quad \psi_i\neq 0,\quad
\langle i|j\rangle_A=\delta_{ij},\quad \langle i|j\rangle_B=\delta_{ij}.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\sum_{i=1}^{N}|\psi_i|^2=1.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\rho_A:=\operatorname{Tr}_B\bigl(|\psi\rangle_{AB}\langle\psi|_{AB}\bigr).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &S(A):=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A\log\rho_A).\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\lambda_i>0,\quad \sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i=1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad -\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\log\lambda_i\leq \log N.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{If the bipartition cuts virtual legs of dimensions }d_1,\ldots,d_k,
\text{ then }N\leq D:=\prod_{j=1}^{k}d_j.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &d_j=\chi\text{ for every cut virtual leg }j=1,\ldots,k.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\chi\geq 1,\quad \log(x^k)=k\log x\text{ for }x>0\text{ and integer }k\geq 0.\\
\text{(P9)}\quad &0<x\leq y\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \log x\leq \log y.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align*}
\rho_A
&=\operatorname{Tr}_B\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}
\psi_i\overline{\psi_j}\,|i\rangle_A |i\rangle_B\langle j|_A\langle j|_B\right)
&&\text{by (P1), (P3)}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}
\psi_i\overline{\psi_j}\,|i\rangle_A\langle j|_A\operatorname{Tr}_B(|i\rangle_B\langle j|_B)
&&\text{linearity of }\operatorname{Tr}_B\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}
\psi_i\overline{\psi_j}\,|i\rangle_A\langle j|_A\langle j|i\rangle_B
&&\text{partial trace over }B\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{N}|\psi_i|^2 |i\rangle_A\langle i|_A
&&\text{by orthonormality in (P1)}.
\end{align*}
Thus the nonzero eigenvalues of \(\rho_A\) are \(\lambda_i:=|\psi_i|^2\). Therefore
\begin{align*}
S(A)
&=-\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\log\lambda_i
&&\text{by (P4) and the eigenvalues above}\\
&\leq \log N
&&\text{by (P2), (P5)}.
\end{align*}
The PEPS cut gives
\begin{align*}
N
&\leq D
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\prod_{j=1}^{k}d_j
&&\text{definition of }D\text{ in (P6)}\\
&=\prod_{j=1}^{k}\chi
&&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=\chi^k.
&&\text{product of }k\text{ equal factors}
\end{align*}
Taking logarithms,
\begin{align*}
\log N
&\leq \log(\chi^k)
&&\text{by (P8), (P9)}\\
&=k\log\chi
&&\text{by (P8)}.
\end{align*}
Combining the two bounds gives
\begin{align*}
S(A)\leq \log N\leq k\log\chi.
&&\text{transitivity of }\leq
\end{align*}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{S(A)\leq \log N\leq k\log\chi}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_2:
\textbf{Claim.} For the gapped continuum corner term
\[
b_A(\theta):=-C\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr),\qquad C>0,
\qquad 0<\theta<\pi,
\]
the two limiting forms are
\[
b_A(\theta)=-\frac{C\pi}{\theta}+O(\theta)\quad(\theta\to 0),
\qquad
b_A(\theta)=-\frac{C}{3}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)\quad(\theta\to\pi).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &b_A(\theta):=-C\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr),\quad C>0,
\quad 0<\theta<\pi.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &g(\theta):=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\cot\theta=\theta^{-1}-\frac{\theta}{3}+O(\theta^3)\quad\text{as }\theta\to 0.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\delta:=\pi-\theta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\cot(\pi-\delta)=-\cot\delta.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\cot\delta=\delta^{-1}-\frac{\delta}{3}-\frac{\delta^3}{45}+O(\delta^5)\quad\text{as }\delta\to 0.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &O(x^m)x^n=O(x^{m+n})\text{ for nonnegative integers }m,n.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &O(x^p)+O(x^q)=O(x^{\min\{p,q\}})\text{ as }x\to0.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
For \(\theta\to0\),
\begin{align*}
g(\theta)
&=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=1+(\pi-\theta)\left(\theta^{-1}-\frac{\theta}{3}+O(\theta^3)\right)
&&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=1+\pi\theta^{-1}-1-\frac{\pi\theta}{3}+\frac{\theta^2}{3}+O(\theta^3)
&&\text{distributivity and (P7)}\\
&=\frac{\pi}{\theta}+O(\theta)
&&\text{by cancellation and (P8)}.
\end{align*}
Substitution into \(b_A\) gives
\begin{align*}
b_A(\theta)
&=-C g(\theta)
&&\text{by (P1), (P2)}\\
&=-C\left(\frac{\pi}{\theta}+O(\theta)\right)
&&\text{previous line}\\
&=-\frac{C\pi}{\theta}+O(\theta)
&&\text{since }C\text{ is constant}.
\end{align*}
For \(\theta\to\pi\), use \(\theta=\pi-\delta\) with \(\delta\to0\):
\begin{align*}
g(\pi-\delta)
&=1+\delta\cot(\pi-\delta)
&&\text{by (P2), (P4)}\\
&=1-\delta\cot\delta
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=1-\delta\left(\delta^{-1}-\frac{\delta}{3}-\frac{\delta^3}{45}+O(\delta^5)\right)
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\frac{\delta^2}{3}+\frac{\delta^4}{45}+O(\delta^6)
&&\text{by distributivity and (P7)}.
\end{align*}
Therefore
\begin{align*}
b_A(\theta)
&=-C g(\pi-\delta)
&&\text{by (P1), (P2), (P4)}\\
&=-C\left(\frac{\delta^2}{3}+\frac{\delta^4}{45}+O(\delta^6)\right)
&&\text{previous line}\\
&=-\frac{C}{3}\delta^2+O(\delta^4)
&&\text{collect powers}\\
&=-\frac{C}{3}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{b_A(\theta)=-\frac{C\pi}{\theta}+O(\theta)\ (\theta\to0),\qquad
b_A(\theta)=-\frac{C}{3}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)\ (\theta\to\pi)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.} In the near-smooth square-lattice counting model with
\[
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta):=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr),
\qquad 2\tan^{-1}(1/2)<\theta<\pi,
\]
the smooth-subtracted skipping probability has the same angular dependence as the continuum corner function:
\[
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi)
=-\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)
=-\frac{1}{12}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)
\quad(\theta\to\pi).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &2\tan^{-1}(1/2)<\theta<\pi.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta):=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &g(\theta):=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\delta:=\pi-\theta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\cot(\pi-\delta)=-\cot\delta.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\cot\delta=\delta^{-1}-\frac{\delta}{3}-\frac{\delta^3}{45}+O(\delta^5)\quad\text{as }\delta\to0.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\lim_{\delta\to0}\delta\cot\delta=1.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &O(x^m)x^n=O(x^{m+n})\text{ for nonnegative integers }m,n.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
First compute the smooth-angle value:
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi)
&:=\lim_{\theta\to\pi}p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)
&&\text{definition of smooth-angle value}\\
&=\lim_{\delta\to0}\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-\delta\cot(\pi-\delta)\bigr)
&&\text{by (P2), (P4)}\\
&=\lim_{\delta\to0}\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1+\delta\cot\delta\bigr)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}
&&\text{by (P7)}.
\end{align*}
Subtracting this value gives
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi)
&=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)-\frac{1}{2}
&&\text{by (P2) and the previous result}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4}(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta-\frac{2}{4}
&&\text{common denominator}\\
&=-\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)
&&\text{factorization}\\
&=-\frac{1}{4}g(\theta)
&&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align*}
Now expand the angular factor for \(\theta=\pi-\delta\):
\begin{align*}
g(\pi-\delta)
&=1+\delta\cot(\pi-\delta)
&&\text{by (P3), (P4)}\\
&=1-\delta\cot\delta
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=1-\delta\left(\delta^{-1}-\frac{\delta}{3}-\frac{\delta^3}{45}+O(\delta^5)\right)
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\frac{\delta^2}{3}+\frac{\delta^4}{45}+O(\delta^6)
&&\text{by distributivity and (P8)}.
\end{align*}
Therefore
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi)
&=-\frac{1}{4}g(\pi-\delta)
&&\text{by the smooth-subtracted formula above}\\
&=-\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{\delta^2}{3}+\frac{\delta^4}{45}+O(\delta^6)\right)
&&\text{previous line}\\
&=-\frac{\delta^2}{12}+O(\delta^4)
&&\text{collect powers}\\
&=-\frac{1}{12}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi)=-\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)=-\frac{1}{12}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\textbf{Claim.} In the near-smooth lattice-corner counting model
\[
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta):=\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta),
\qquad
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta):=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr),
\]
the lattice-corner contribution obeys
\[
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)=-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^2\bigr),
\]
and its smooth-subtracted form is
\[
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi)
=-\frac{1}{3}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)
\quad(\theta\to\pi).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &2\tan^{-1}(1/2)<\theta<\pi.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta):=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta):=\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\delta:=\pi-\theta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\cot(\pi-\delta)=-\cot\delta.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\cot\delta=\delta^{-1}-\frac{\delta}{3}-\frac{\delta^3}{45}+O(\delta^5)\quad\text{as }\delta\to0.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\log(\cos\delta)=-\frac{\delta^2}{2}-\frac{\delta^4}{12}+O(\delta^6)\quad\text{as }\delta\to0.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &O(x^m)x^n=O(x^{m+n})\text{ for nonnegative integers }m,n.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
The paper's near-smooth relation follows immediately after isolating the logarithmic term:
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)
&=\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)
&&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\log(\cos\delta)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\left(-\frac{\delta^2}{2}-\frac{\delta^4}{12}+O(\delta^6)\right)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)
&&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)+O(\delta^2)
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^2\bigr)
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align*}
For the smooth-subtracted form, first expand \(p_{\mathrm{skip}}\):
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi-\delta)
&=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1-\delta\cot(\pi-\delta)\bigr)
&&\text{by (P2), (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\bigl(1+\delta\cot\delta\bigr)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\delta\left(\delta^{-1}-\frac{\delta}{3}-\frac{\delta^3}{45}+O(\delta^5)\right)\right)
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\delta^2}{12}-\frac{\delta^4}{180}+O(\delta^6)
&&\text{by distributivity and (P8)}.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi-\delta)
&=\log(\cos\delta)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi-\delta)
&&\text{by (P3), (P4)}\\
&=\left(-\frac{\delta^2}{2}-\frac{\delta^4}{12}+O(\delta^6)\right)
-2\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\delta^2}{12}-\frac{\delta^4}{180}+O(\delta^6)\right)
&&\text{by (P7) and previous line}\\
&=-1-\frac{\delta^2}{3}-\frac{13\delta^4}{180}+O(\delta^6)
&&\text{collect powers}.
\end{align*}
The smooth-angle value is
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi)
&:=\lim_{\delta\to0}p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi-\delta)
&&\text{definition of smooth-angle value}\\
&=-1
&&\text{previous line}.
\end{align*}
Therefore
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi)
&=p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi-\delta)+1
&&\text{by (P4) and }p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi)=-1\\
&=-\frac{\delta^2}{3}-\frac{13\delta^4}{180}+O(\delta^6)
&&\text{substitution}\\
&=-\frac{1}{3}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)=-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^2\bigr),\qquad
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi)=-\frac{1}{3}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.} Suppose the orientation- and origin-averaged number of crossed lattice objects of type \(x\in\{\mathrm{legs},\mathrm{corners}\}\) has the fitted form
\[
n_x(\theta,r)=\alpha_x(r)+\beta_x(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta,
\]
where \(\partial\beta_x/\partial r=0\). If each crossed object contributes a uniform multiplicative factor \(\chi_x>0\) to the counting bound, then the logarithm of the corresponding counting factor is
\[
\log D_x(\theta,r)=\alpha_x(r)\log\chi_x+\beta_x\log\chi_x\,(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta,
\]
and the coefficient of the angular term is independent of \(r\):
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\bigl(\beta_x\log\chi_x\bigr)=0.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &x\in\{\mathrm{legs},\mathrm{corners}\}.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &D_x(\theta,r):=\chi_x^{\,n_x(\theta,r)}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\chi_x>0\text{ is uniform and independent of }\theta\text{ and }r.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &h(\theta):=(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &n_x(\theta,r)=\alpha_x(r)+\beta_x h(\theta).\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\frac{\partial\beta_x}{\partial r}=0.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\log\chi_x=0.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\log(a^b)=b\log a\quad\text{for }a>0.\\
\text{(P9)}\quad &\frac{\partial}{\partial r}(uv)=\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}v+u\frac{\partial v}{\partial r}.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align*}
\log D_x(\theta,r)
&=\log\left(\chi_x^{\,n_x(\theta,r)}\right)
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=n_x(\theta,r)\log\chi_x
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=\bigl(\alpha_x(r)+\beta_x h(\theta)\bigr)\log\chi_x
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\alpha_x(r)\log\chi_x+\beta_x h(\theta)\log\chi_x
&&\text{distributivity}\\
&=\alpha_x(r)\log\chi_x+\beta_x\log\chi_x\,(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align*}
The angular coefficient is \(\beta_x\log\chi_x\). Its radius derivative is
\begin{align*}
\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\bigl(\beta_x\log\chi_x\bigr)
&=\left(\frac{\partial\beta_x}{\partial r}\right)\log\chi_x
+\beta_x\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\log\chi_x
&&\text{by (P9)}\\
&=0\cdot\log\chi_x+\beta_x\cdot0
&&\text{by (P6), (P7)}\\
&=0.
&&\text{algebra}
\end{align*}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\log D_x(\theta,r)=\alpha_x(r)\log\chi_x+\beta_x\log\chi_x\,(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta,
\qquad \frac{\partial}{\partial r}\bigl(\beta_x\log\chi_x\bigr)=0}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Claim.} A corner term obtained only from a fixed-radius lattice counting region near the apex cannot reproduce the critical-system scaling
\[
K\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)\log |\partial A|
\]
for all boundary lengths \(|\partial A|>0\), unless \(K=0\) or \(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta=0\). Thus an area-independent counting contribution cannot by itself account for a nonzero logarithmic critical corner term.

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &L:=|\partial A|>0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &c_{\mathrm{count}}(\theta,L):=q(\theta).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &c_{\mathrm{crit}}(\theta,L):=K g(\theta)\log L.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &g(\theta):=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{If }c_{\mathrm{count}}(\theta,L)=c_{\mathrm{crit}}(\theta,L)
\text{ for all }L>0,\text{ then }\frac{\partial c_{\mathrm{count}}}{\partial L}=\frac{\partial c_{\mathrm{crit}}}{\partial L}
\text{ for all }L>0.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\frac{\partial}{\partial L}q(\theta)=0\text{ because }q(\theta)\text{ is independent of }L.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\frac{\partial}{\partial L}\log L=L^{-1}\text{ for }L>0.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &L^{-1}\neq0\text{ for }L>0.\\
\text{(P9)}\quad &ab=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a=0\text{ or }b=0.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
Assume equality of the two forms for all \(L>0\). Then
\begin{align*}
c_{\mathrm{count}}(\theta,L)
&=c_{\mathrm{crit}}(\theta,L)
&&\text{assumption}\\
q(\theta)
&=K g(\theta)\log L
&&\text{by (P2), (P3)}.
\end{align*}
Differentiate with respect to \(L\):
\begin{align*}
\frac{\partial c_{\mathrm{count}}}{\partial L}
&=\frac{\partial c_{\mathrm{crit}}}{\partial L}
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
0
&=\frac{\partial}{\partial L}\bigl(Kg(\theta)\log L\bigr)
&&\text{by (P3), (P6)}\\
0
&=Kg(\theta)\frac{\partial}{\partial L}\log L
&&\text{since }K\text{ and }g(\theta)\text{ are independent of }L\\
0
&=Kg(\theta)L^{-1}
&&\text{by (P7)}.
\end{align*}
Because \(L^{-1}\neq0\),
\begin{align*}
Kg(\theta)L^{-1}=0
&\Longrightarrow Kg(\theta)=0
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&\Longrightarrow K=0\text{ or }g(\theta)=0
&&\text{by (P9)}\\
&\Longrightarrow K=0\text{ or }1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta=0
&&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, if \(K\neq0\) and \(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\neq0\), the equality cannot hold for all \(L>0\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{q(\theta)\not\equiv K\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)\log |\partial A|\text{ for all }|\partial A|>0\text{ unless }K=0\text{ or }1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta=0}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
